title: Meeting Armstrong in 1936 and booking the All Stars in Philadelphia
summary: Rose meets Armstrong backstage in Philadelphia in 1936, then promotes the All Stars for $2,500 and later $4,000, and Panassie calls about Nice.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Oh, there were a lot of things, but I don't remember specifically because I haven't read it in years. Yeah. But, what I was thinking of, you know, was that we would talk probably about the, whatever was the extent of my own personal contact with Louis in whatever circumstances. Yeah. And the, see I really didn't know Louis until up north, I never knew him here in New Orleans.
And so, the first time I ever met him was in the backstage at the Nixon's Grand Theater in Philadelphia, which is right across the street from Temple University.

And it was a black theater and I used to come out of, out of class and go across the street to the theater all the time, because I knew a lot of the musicians that were, that were playing in the, in the show. And it was during the time when I had first started doing jazz concerts. So it was 1936 and I went backstage, because his band was playing there. And I knew Louis Russell and Red Allen and people that were playing there, Al Nicholas. So, I had, I had met Louis before, I don't actually remember when, but when, when I went backstage, Albert went to introduce me to him. And Louis says, I know this guy, he's the one that Yubi calls Shazam. So, so that, so he identified me with Yubi at that point. And so, I don't remember that we talked about much then, but I, I sat out front and listened to the, to the music. And Baby Dodds and Pops Foster were in the band and I knew them well. They had already worked for me a number of times. So, anyway, that was the first time I met Louis. Second time I met him was about three years later. And that was backstage at the Oriental Theater in Chicago, where the band was playing. And, again, it was the same band then. The next time I saw him in the Oriental Theater was in 1947, I guess. But, when they started the All Stars. Right. Joe Glazer called me. Joe Glazer was a doll. I loved him. But he called me from New York and, at that time, I was running regular Friday concerts in the Academy of Music in Philadelphia. And he said, well, he said, we put together this band of All Stars. And, with Louis Armstrong. And he told me, Jack Teagarden, Barney Begard, and Sidney Catlett. And, the only one I didn't know was Arwell Shaw, who was a kid. And he said, do you want them in Philadelphia? We're going through to the west coast. And I said, well, how much? So, he says, it'll cost you $2,500. Now, I have to tell you that $2,500 in those days. What year were we talking about? What year were we talking about? We were talking about, I guess, 1946. Astronomical numbers. Because those were hard times for musicians. And I was hiring people like Sidney Bechet and Muggsy Spanier, you know, for my regular concerts. And the top price I ever paid anybody was $35. And that was more than anybody else paid. So, it was bad. You get Sidney Bechet for $35. Oh, sure. And anyway, but still, I had a big following in Philadelphia on a mailing list and all that. And I couldn't afford to have Louis go through there on anybody else's auspices. So, I said, okay, I'll take him, John. He says, you won't be sorry. He said, you better take him now because on our way back, when he comes back, it's going to be $4,000. So, I said, okay. So, sure enough, the band shows up and packed the house, upscale prices and everything. And I made a mint on that concert. So, when Louis came back through on his way back, you know, Joe called me, he said, we're on our way back. It's $4,000. I said, it's fine. And from then on, you know, it was kind of upscale for jazz concerts and Louis especially. Mm-hmm. Anyway, Louis came back and I didn't see him very much during the concert time because that's too confused. Yeah. And, but in the meantime, I had gotten a call from Panassier. And Panassier was interested in doing the Nice Festival, which was his first adventure into anything like that. Not that year, but I mean, he was, so anyway. Mm-hmm.
